title: The Future of AI Shopping Depends on Trust
gist: Oxford Economics and Synchrony argue AI shopping is moving from assisted discovery to agentic commerce, where agents complete purchases, making consumer trust (protection, control, final approval) the key adoption gate. Morgan Stanley sizes AI shopping agents at 10-20% of US e-commerce by 2030 ($190bn-$385bn), with early trust and standard-setters best positioned.

insights.claim: Online shopping is shifting from a self-directed activity to one where AI agents shop and complete purchases on a consumer's behalf within consumer-set parameters, beyond generative AI's current role in discovery and price comparison.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Value capture in e-commerce may migrate toward whoever controls the agent layer that executes transactions.
insights.quote: The next step is agentic commerce, where AI agents shop on a consumer’s behalf, including completing the purchase
insights.locator: AI is starting to change online

insights.claim: When an AI agent executes a purchase, the consumer delegates judgment, money, identity and permission to act, so trust requirements rise sharply versus AI-assisted comparison where the shopper still decides.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Adoption of agentic shopping hinges on trust infrastructure, not just model capability.

insights.claim: The more autonomy an AI shopping agent has, the more confidence consumers need before using it, specifically assurance it acts in their interest, protects information and money, follows their rules, and offers a clear way to fix mistakes.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Providers of identity, fraud protection, spending controls and dispute resolution for agents could see rising demand.

insights.claim: A Synchrony survey of 2,000 US consumers in May 2026 found consumers open to letting AI do more for them, but only when they feel protected, in control, and able to approve the final decision.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Near-term agentic commerce likely to run with human-approval checkpoints, limiting fully autonomous purchasing at first.
insights.quote: consumers are opento letting AI do more for them, but only when they feel protected, in control, and able toapprove the final decision

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley estimates AI shopping agents could account for 10% to 20% of US e-commerce by 2030, equal to $190 billion to $385 billion in annual spending.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: A sizable new spending channel for payments networks, retailers and platforms within about four years.
insights.locator: The market opportunity for agentic commerce

insights.claim: Companies that establish consumer trust early and set the standards for agentic transactions may be best positioned to shape the development of the agentic commerce market.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Early standard-setters among payments firms and platforms may gain durable moats in agent-driven transactions.
insights.locator: The market opportunity for agentic commerce

insights.claim: Consumers will choose which brands, platforms and financial providers they trust to make AI shopping feel safe, clear and accountable, making trust a competitive differentiator across retail and payments.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Financial providers like Synchrony are positioning trust and protection as their selling point in agentic payments.
insights.locator: The market opportunity for agentic commerce
